boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten Kenyon places whose everyday uses extend beyond their façades—from reservable study rooms and student-run performance space to trails, community centers and a campus game room.

cards.title: Match the Room to the Work
cards.subtitle: Open, quiet and group-study options inside Chalmers Library
cards.notes: Use the first-come seating for solo work, choose Levels 1 or 3 for quiet, or reserve a group room when collaboration needs a screen.
cards.short_summary: Chalmers supports several study modes instead of treating the entire library as one uniform workspace.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon Libraries states that Chalmers has open study spaces on every floor, quiet reading rooms on Levels 1 and 3, and reservable group rooms on Levels 1 through 4.
cards.access_notes: Open study seating is first-come, first-served. Group rooms may be reserved or used on a walk-up basis when available; current building access rules apply.

cards.title: Look Beyond the Fitness Floor
cards.subtitle: Recreation, study lounges and screenings share one building
cards.notes: Check the building’s current schedule, then pair a workout with a study-lounge stop or look for a film screening in the theater.
cards.short_summary: Lowry combines exercise facilities with quieter social and academic uses under the same roof.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon describes the Lowry Center as containing a pool, track, courts, fitness and dance rooms, study lounges and a movie theater.
cards.access_notes: Facility access and activity availability vary by the Lowry Center’s current schedule and campus eligibility rules.

cards.title: Follow Student-Led Programming
cards.subtitle: A social and programming space serving all Kenyon students
cards.notes: Watch campus event listings for discussions, films and cultural programs; respect the residential portion and any event-specific boundaries.
cards.short_summary: Snowden’s public-facing role includes student-guided cultural programming alongside its residential function.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon states that Snowden provides programming and social space for all Kenyon students, with events guided by student managers and student leaders.
cards.access_notes: Attend publicized programs or use the center according to campus guidance; private residential rooms are not general-access spaces.

cards.title: Find the 24-Hour Community Space
cards.subtitle: Student-managed space for LGBTQ programming and events
cards.notes: Use the shared space for community programming and connection, while treating residents’ rooms and posted event boundaries as private.
cards.short_summary: Unity House pairs student management with around-the-clock community space focused on LGBTQ life at Kenyon.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon identifies Unity House as a student-managed, safe 24-hour space committed to LGBTQ programming and events.
cards.access_notes: The official page describes a 24-hour space; follow current K-Card, program-house and residential access expectations.

cards.title: See What Students Put Onstage
cards.subtitle: A student-run arts and performance space in a small barn
cards.notes: Check the student events calendar before walking over; the two floors support performances, community time and rehearsal activity.
cards.short_summary: The Horn gives students responsibility for a venue that accommodates performance, gathering and practice.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon describes the Horn Gallery as a student-run arts and performance space with a performance venue, community space and practice room.
cards.access_notes: Entry depends on scheduled events and current campus access rules; consult official event information before visiting.

cards.title: Choose a Dining Room by Mood
cards.subtitle: Three distinct student dining rooms inside Peirce Hall
cards.notes: Look past the servery and compare Great Hall, bright Thomas Hall and the downstairs Alumni Dining Room before choosing a table.
cards.short_summary: Peirce divides the shared dining experience among three rooms with markedly different settings.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon states that Peirce Hall has three large dining rooms: Great Hall, Thomas Hall and the downstairs Alumni Dining Room.
cards.access_notes: Dining access follows current meal-plan, guest and operating policies; some rooms may be assigned to scheduled events.

cards.title: Use the Path as a Pause Point
cards.subtitle: Kenyon’s central footpath also functions as shared gathering space
cards.notes: Walk it as the campus connector, but use the benches and wider gathering areas when stopping so through traffic can keep moving.
cards.short_summary: Middle Path is both practical circulation and a place for informal encounters across campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon describes Middle Path as a footpath, village green, gathering space and marketplace that runs the length of campus.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus path; remain aware of weather, maintenance and College rules for organized gatherings or demonstrations.

cards.title: Pick a Trail Before You Arrive
cards.subtitle: More than 10 miles of daylight-access preserve trails
cards.notes: Open the official trail guide first, choose a route suited to conditions and daylight, and carry out everything you bring into the preserve.
cards.short_summary: The BFEC gives students a nearby setting for self-guided walking, nature observation and field-based learning.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon states that the 700-acre BFEC has more than 10 miles of trails and is open to the public seven days a week during daylight hours.
cards.source_title: Brown Family Environmental Center | Kenyon College
cards.access_notes: Open to the public seven days a week during daylight hours. Check official trail guidance and seasonal conditions before setting out.

cards.title: Join the Farm Through a Real Role
cards.subtitle: Students participate as volunteers, workers, interns and class visitors
cards.notes: Contact the farm about a defined volunteer, work or class opportunity rather than entering animal or production areas without guidance.
cards.short_summary: Kenyon Farm is a working educational site where student participation takes several organized forms.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon says students engage with the farm as volunteers, workers and summer interns, while classes visit for tours and hands-on activities.
cards.access_notes: A working farm is not unrestricted space. Arrange participation or a visit through the farm and follow staff directions around animals and equipment.

cards.title: Reset With a Shared Game
cards.subtitle: Arcade games, tables, seating and a borrowable console
cards.notes: Bring a friend or join a casual game, share equipment considerately and confirm current building access before planning a longer session.
cards.short_summary: The renovated game room gives students a low-structure indoor option for social time away from classwork.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon reports that the Gund Commons game room includes arcade games, foosball, ping pong, two pool tables, comfortable seating and a Nintendo Switch students can borrow.
cards.source_title: Collaboration Is the Name of the Game | Kenyon College
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to current Gund Commons hours, campus access rules and equipment-borrowing procedures.
